Commentary.Commentary: South Africa will be pretty much pleased with their efforts today. Everything clicked in their favour and now would be looking to seal the series when they meet next in Durban on the 5th of October, 2016 at 1700 IST. Will Australia come back hard? Let's wait and find out. Until next time, it's goodbye from us. Have a happy week ahead!

Right then! Another run-feast was expected but turned out to be a lop-sided one in the end. Australia now have a huge task ahead of them as they can't afford to put any foot wrong if they are to keep this series alive.

Man of the match and South African captain FAF DU PLESSIS says that it was an amazing game of cricket. Adds that they were almost perfect in their batting and bowling performance. Says that the guys laid down the base really well and the bowlers maintained great intensity on a good Wanderers pitch. Opines that their play was of exceptional quality, with crazy good openers. Says that they kept up fantastic pressure with the new ball which allowed them to take three early wicket. He says that they learnt from their mistakes. (On the pitch) Says that there was a bit of bounce but as they waited for the ball to get softer. (As Man of the Match) Says that it was a great day and that he felt good scoring. (On getting hit on the thumb) Says that he is lucky to not use his left hand much as he uses his bottom hand but it was nice to get a hundred. Repeats that it was a good wicket with extra bounce and they had very good shot selection and timed their innings well. Ends by thanking a wonderful Wanderers stadium for their support.

AUSTRALIAN SKIPPER STEVEN SMITH says 330-340 could be well under their reach as far as the history of the ground is concerned. Feels they didn't really got going with the bat and then with the ball, he accepts that this inexperience cost them as part of a new learning curve. Further says, his bowlers pulled off towards the end but still feels the damage was already done till then. Appreciates du Plessis and Duminy and admits it's difficult to stop them once they get into the groove. Ends by saying the Aussies are known to come out well when they have their backs to the wall. Hopes they win the next one as each game from here on is a must-win one for them.

Earlier in the day, stand-in captain du Plessis helped his side to 361 with his century. Duminy was in a hurry too, racking up 82 in 58 balls.  The Australians bowled well but gave away runs in the middle. Hastings and Marsh were the main wicket-takers. The bowlers did manage to reign South Africa back in towards the end but the runs were already on the scoreboard by then.

South Africa's bowling was superlative, picking up wickets at regular intervals and never letting Australia rest easy for a moment. They made wonderful use of the bounce on offer and forced the Aussies to scrape together singles despite chasing a mammoth target. Once again, Rabada and Steyn impressed with their bowling, picking up a brace each, but the fiery Parnell was the pick for his 3-fer.

Australia continued to lose wickets steadily, unable to sustain a partnership for any length of time. Head and Wade managed to establish a 69-run partnership, by far the highest of their innings but the damage was done by then. Head scored 51 before being dismissed. Hastings made a hurried cameo but nothing would have saved Australia at that point.

Folks around the stadium rejoice as Australia's struggle finally comes to a close. From the moment the South African bowlers took to the crease, the pitch looked like a dramatically different one. The Australian openers got off to a slow start which was compounded by the loss of Finch early on. Skipper Smith hung in there but fell to an amazing catch by keeper de Kock. Warner stuck it out to score a well-earned half-century but was dismissed the very next ball.

OUT! You miss and I hit! Phehlekwayo cleans it up after being taken to the cleaners. Hurls it on a length and on off, Zampa looks to cut by making some room only to miss it as the ball goes on to disturb the furniture behind. Just short! Another short ball outside off, Zampa looks to cut but is lucky as the ball falls short of Rossouw at point.

In the corridor outside off, Hastings looks to play it but misses.

Fuller length delivery on off, John drives it towards covers.
Short and down the leg side, Hastings ducks to evade it.
Length ball outside off, Hastings shows the  full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot. The fielder goes for a direct hit but misses the stumps. They pick up a single.
Full and a tad outside off, pushed to the covers.

Fuller ball on the pads, flicked towards mid-wicket where Miller makes a diving stop to only give away a single

The umpire has a long think and raises his finger but Head has his doubts. Australia can't afford to lose any more wicket and he decides to review it. The snicko meter shows that there wasn't an edge and hotspot confirms that the ball would go on to clip the leg stump. Things are looking nigh impossible for Australia now.
Head is adjudged LBW but he opts for the review straightaway. Looks out though.
Maiden ODI fifty for Travis Head!

FOUR! 50 FOR TRAVIS HEAD! Fantastic play from Head when Australia needed him. An uncalled for short delivery around off and Head pulls it over mid-wicket for a might boundary. That was a fantastic way to bring in his half-century.
Back of a length delivery, Head gets up on his toes to play that one.

50-run stand between Travis Head and Matthew Wade.

FOUR! Edged away! Touch short and outside off, it stays low as well. Head looks to slash but the ball meets the bottom edge and runs down to third man for a boundary. Head is really playing well here.
Beaten! On a length and outside off, with some extra bounce off the deck. Head looks to cut but fails to put any bat on it.

Flattish on middle, punched down to long on for a single.
Loopy delivery around middle and off, Matthew defends it off the front foot.
On middle and leg, Head nurdles  it through mid-wicket for a single.

Length ball outside off, dabbed to backward point for a single.

Welcome back to the Wanderers for the run chase. Australia need 362 runs to win. The players are back on the field with DAVID WARNER and AARON FINCH set to open the batting. DALE STEYN will be starting the bowling proceedings. Here we go...
